body.x: Futureduck Inc. (CEO Joy Kibbeum Na) announced its participation in the Global Media Online Meet-Up held on July 3 in partnership with U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, targeting Korean startups and businesses.

This Global Media Meet-Up, co-hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, aims to introduce Korean startups and their products and technologies to the global market. It focuses on promoting companies applying for the CES 2026 Innovation Awards and securing early global media exposure and business opportunities.

Founded in February 2024 by IT and education experts, Futureduck is an edtech startup whose mission is “to cultivate independent thinkers.” In October 2023, it launched its writing education platform ‘Quewrite’, which supports students’ critical thinking and literacy development.

Quewrite is a platform that helps students complete the entire writing process independently through an AI tutor that asks guiding questions. It supports students who struggle with writing by helping them organize and articulate their thoughts, and also assists teachers in addressing practical challenges in writing instruction at schools and academies.

Futureduck is currently developing ‘Que:read’, a literacy education platform that expands the philosophy and technology of Quewrite into the domain of reading. Que:read is set for release in February 2026 and will form the foundation of a next-generation integrated literacy education platform alongside Quewrite.

body.cap: Promotional banner for Futureduck’s AI-based reading support platform ‘Que:read’ | Image provided by Futureduck

body.x: The beta version of Quewrite is currently being tested for educational effectiveness at 32 schools across Korea, involving 1,056 teachers and students. These trials are helping verify the platform’s practicality and efficacy in real classroom settings. Futureduck is incorporating positive feedback to enhance the platform further.

With a major update planned for late 2025, the company will officially launch commercial operations and expand its presence in both public and private education markets. With the growing demand for literacy instruction, Quewrite is quickly gaining traction as a practical teaching tool.

Based on its domestic user references, Futureduck is also preparing to enter overseas markets, focusing on Southeast Asia and North America. The company emphasizes that Quewrite’s multilingual adaptability and pedagogical design offer a competitive edge in global education markets. Futureduck aims to become a key partner in closing global literacy gaps.

Currently under development, Que:read is an AI-powered conversational reading support platform. It provides customized, dialogue-based questions before, during, and after reading to help users understand texts and deepen their thinking. Going beyond simple comprehension tools, Que:read diagnoses and improves users’ literacy as an intelligent reading companion.

Technologically, Que:read stands out with its conversational diagnostic capabilities, which allow it to identify weak literacy areas through natural dialogue. Leveraging advanced NLP and speech recognition, the platform offers real-time personalized learning guidance.

body.cap: Joy Kibbeum Na, CEO of Futureduck, and Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, pose for a commemorative photo during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The user-friendly, aesthetically refined interface features voice interaction, optimized screen layout, and text display for comfortable long-term reading. Que:read’s most innovative feature is its AI philosophy: unlike traditional AI that limits thinking, it supports deeper, more critical, and creative thought.

Its design promotes cognitive growth through questions that foster critical and interpretive thinking. Globally, Que:read aims to tackle widespread literacy deficiencies. Its voice interface and personalized diagnostics will allow early learners and those in underserved regions to access high-quality reading education, contributing to educational equity.

Futureduck is entering the CES Innovation Awards for the first time, officially unveiling its flagship AI-based literacy platform, Quewrite, to the global market. More than just a competition, this is a strategic opportunity to validate the company’s competitiveness in the global edtech sector. Futureduck views CES as a turning point for expanding partnerships and international reach, connecting with global buyers, education policymakers, and investors.

Target markets include North America, the UK, Singapore, and Vietnam—regions with high digital device penetration, strong classroom tech integration, and educational systems that value inquiry-based learning, critical thinking, and literacy. These environments are well-suited for Que:read and Quewrite.

Another key strategy is collaboration with education publishers and curriculum providers—critical partners and buyers who are actively seeking innovative digital solutions. Futureduck believes Que:read and Quewrite meet their needs and can quickly reach more students through such partnerships.

body.cap: Q&A session between Ubergizmo and Futureduck during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Futureduck plans to integrate Quewrite and Que:read into a comprehensive literacy education platform that connects reading and writing instruction in the classroom. The platform will offer precision support for individual literacy development.

The company is also developing AI-based diagnostic engines that assess not only literacy components but also categorize types of thinking skills. This will evolve the platform from an educational content provider into a ‘learning companion’ that diagnoses students’ cognitive and expressive abilities and guides their growth.

In Korea, Futureduck is actively engaging with teachers and schools through various educational expos and academic conferences. For international expansion, the company plans to participate in major global exhibitions such as the BETT Show in the UK, the ISTE Conference in the U.S., and EduTech Asia in Singapore. These efforts aim to raise global brand awareness and build partnerships with overseas education stakeholders.

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
